demand.reason: Global platinum mine production was about 170 metric tons in 2025, placing it within the negligible-demand band of ≤500 tons.

growth.reason: Demand projects a low, steady growth trajectory (1-5% CAGR). Maturing automotive catalytic uses and stable industrial base loads offset the emerging, low-volume requirements from the clean hydrogen economy.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: South Africa controls approximately 71% of global primary extraction, placing primary mining diversity in the concentrated 65–85% band (Score 4).


Refining: Downstream refinement is heavily integrated with primary South African mine output. South African refiners pace global market share synchronously with extraction, matching the 65–85% band (Score 4).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Global PGM resources exceed 81,000 metric tons. Against current extraction rates, known reserves represent centuries of supply, which is effectively limitless (>100 years).


Diversification: Total global reserves yield a calculated HHI of about 0.70. Because South Africa controls about 83% of the reserve base, the geographic endowment matches the highly concentrated maximum score.

end_use.reason:
Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): acts as the core electrocatalyst in PEM fuel cells for hydrogen production. Defense & National Security (+1.5): structurally foundational for military-grade sensors and turbine hardware. Healthcare & Biomedical (+1.0): utilized widely across essential chemotherapy drugs and pacemakers. Advanced Semiconductors & Computing (+1.0): forms critical electrical contacts in hard-disk drives and thermocouples. Electrification & Transport (+1.0): deployed pervasively in automotive catalytic converters. Construction & Heavy Industry (+0.5): serves as an essential chemical processing catalyst and glass-fiber bushing.


Sector presence scores total 6.5 across 6 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +2.5, yielding an objective composite score of 9.0.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Palladium acts as a commercially deployed substitute within automotive catalytic converters depending on pricing dynamics, matching the criteria where substitutions are commercially deployed with manageable trade-offs (Score 2).


Recyclability: Global secondary production from autocatalysts and industrial applications is highly mature. Recycled scrap supplies 25-33% of consumption, pacing securely in the >40% high recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Platinum extraction requires deep, hazardous shaft mining in the Bushveld Complex followed by smelting and highly complex, multi-stage solvent extraction separations, characterizing it as highly specialized and chemically demanding.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is adequate but constrained. While South African output contracts under power grid failures, advanced expansions (Waterberg, Platreef) and Zimbabwean assets are capable of adding 10–20% to supply within 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India possesses no commercial domestic extraction of platinum, leaving its automotive and industrial catalytic sectors 100% import-dependent (Score 5).


Strategic Posture: Platinum is recognized on India's critical minerals list, and Hindustan Platinum (an LBMA/LPPM good-delivery refiner) and others recover PGMs from spent catalysts; the ₹1,500 crore recycling scheme (2025) covers catalytic converters. Lacking binding overseas KABIL equity stakes, the posture aligns with early-stage declared strategic intent (Score 3).

price_volatility.reason: Platinum prices exhibited moderate volatility, fluctuating steadily between roughly $886/oz and $1,495/oz over a five-year cycle. Multi-year swings pace cleanly within a 50–100% variance band without complete supply-side breakdown.

capability.name: Platinum
capability.next_move: Grow recycling: secure spent catalysts and scrapped converters for Indian refiners, and assess the Boula-Nuasahi deposit.
capability.what_india_has: Hindustan Platinum (founded 1961) refines platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium from spent catalysts and says it is at peak production; Ravindra Heraeus recycles catalysts at Udaipur; Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India; a Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme covers catalytic converters. Resources of 20.92 t of platinum-group metals, 67% in Odisha.

stages.world: South Africa 120 of 170 t (2025); Russia 20 t; Zimbabwe 18 t.
stages.india: None. Boula-Nuasahi in Odisha is the only proven deposit.

stages.world: Smelters and precious-metal refineries beside the mines in South Africa and Russia; recyclers elsewhere.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum and Ravindra Heraeus refine spent catalysts.
Johnson Matthey (Manesar, 25 million autocatalysts made by 2014) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts with imported metal.

stages.world: Catalytic converters, jewellery, chemical and glass plant, hydrogen fuel cells.
stages.india: Primary metal is entirely imported (IBM); vehicle catalysts and jewellery.

strategyList.name: Recycling (batteries, magnets, catalysts, PV)
strategyList.what: Shredding and hydrometallurgy of black mass; magnet recovery; spent-catalyst leaching; PV-panel recovery.
strategyList.outside_china: Battery recycling: China has over three-quarters of pre-treatment and 90% of material-recovery capacity; Europe, Japan, Korea and the US smaller.
strategyList.cost: India's scheme expects ~Rs 8,000 crore for 270+ kt/yr of capacity (~Rs 30 crore per kt/yr), yielding ~40 kt/yr of critical minerals.
strategyList.india_base: Lohum, Rubamin, the Bhopal magnet facility, CSIR-NML; Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme (2025).

chemistryList.name: Catalysts and spent-catalyst recovery
chemistryList.who: Rubamin (Mo, Co, Ni from spent catalyst); Hindustan Platinum (PGM refining).
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Molybdenum and cobalt recovery; catalyst-grade chemicals.
chemistryList.summary: Spent catalysts are concentrated secondary sources of useful metals. India already has industrial experience recovering molybdenum and other metals, alongside precious-metal refining. The opportunity is to connect traceable waste collection, selective recovery and customer-approved products, while distinguishing regeneration from destruction and metal recovery.

links.how: Hindustan Platinum makes precious-metal catalysts and recovers platinum-group metals from used ones; it names platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium among the metals it refines.
